title: Senior Security Engineer
description:
About Kestra

Kestra is the universal orchestration platform : open source, declarative, and designed to orchestrate data pipelines, IT automation, business workflows, and AI/agentic systems.

Trusted by over 10,000 organizations worldwide , including JPMorgan Chase, Bloomberg, FILA, and Crédit Agricole , Kestra orchestrates mission-critical workloads at scale. The open-source project has close to 30,000 GitHub stars , hundreds of contributors, and a fast-growing global community.

About the role

Kestra runs arbitrary, user-defined code at scale. Our users write workflows that execute scripts, containers, and queries against their own production systems, through hundreds of community-built plugins, on a platform whose entire source code is public. That is an unusually rich attack surface, and securing it is a genuinely hard engineering problem rather than a checklist exercise.
You would be our first dedicated security hire. We're looking for a Senior Security Engineer to own and elevate the end-to-end security posture of our platform, infrastructure, and open-source ecosystem.
This is a unique, hybrid role for someone who excels at both sides of security: actively breaking systems to find vulnerabilities (hands-on penetration testing) and actively fixing them (opening PRs, patching infrastructure, and managing supply chain risks). If you want to build a world-class security foundation for a fast-growing open-source and SaaS platform, this role is for you.
This is a hands-on engineering role, not a GRC or compliance one. 

What you would do

Your first six months would focus on the first three points below. The rest is where the role grows.

- Conduct hands-on penetration testing and threat modeling across our web application, APIs, control plane, and cloud environments.

- Manage end-to-end vulnerability tracking across our codebases, software dependencies (SCA), container images, and cloud infrastructure.

- Proactively fix security flaws by writing patches, submitting Pull Requests (PRs), or collaborating directly with product teams to guide remediation.

- Audit and harden our cloud infrastructure (GCP, Kubernetes clusters, and networking configurations) against external and internal threats.

- Automate security tooling into our CI/CD pipelines (SAST, DAST, dependency scanners) to catch CVEs before code reaches production.

- Perform security code reviews and evaluate third-party dependencies, open-source integrations, and supply-chain risks.

- Lead incident response efforts and establish continuous monitoring, detection, and mitigation strategies.

- Own our public security posture as an open-source project: vulnerability disclosure process, CVE handling, security advisories, and the trust model of our plugin ecosystem.

Our Tech Stack

- Security & Vulnerability Tools : Trivy, GitHub Security / Dependabot, Elastic Security 

- Infrastructure : Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform

- Cloud : GCP

- Programming language : Java, Typescript, Javascript

- Datastore : PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch

- Queuing : Redis, Kafka, AMQP

- Monitoring & Logs : ELK, Prometheus, Grafana

- Deployment & Repository : GitHub Actions, ArgoCD

What we are looking for

- 5+ years of experience in Security Engineering, Product Security, DevSecOps, or a combined Offensive/Defensive role.

- Strong hands-on penetration testing background , with proven ability to discover application, API, and network-level vulnerabilities.

- A builder/fixer mindset : You don't just export scanner PDFs; you can read code, understand exploits, write fixes, or provide clear remediation steps to engineers.

- Deep familiarity with cloud security (AWS or GCP) and containerized environments ( Kubernetes , Docker).

- Experience with dependency and supply-chain security (CVE management, open-source licensing, SCA tools).

- Fluent in English and comfortable working autonomously in a fully remote environment.

- Adaptability to a fast-paced open-source startup environment where pragmatism and execution speed matter.

Perks & Benefits

description:
About Notabene 

Notabene is on a mission to make crypto a part of the everyday economy. Leading crypto organizations use our tools to reduce transaction risk and make crypto transfers safe. Working across three continents in eight countries, the Notabene team serves our fantastic community of 100+ customers, including financial institutions, fintechs, exchanges, and more. Our co-founders spearheaded foundational Self Sovereign Identity protocols and use-cases. This technology is key to the internals of our cutting edge tech stack.

We’re proud to have the support of leading investors, including Y Combinator, Jump Capital, Castle Island, Green Visor Capital, and more.

We’re at an exhilarating moment in our journey, as regulation technologies (reg-techs) are fast becoming recognized as a vital enabler of the crypto ecosystem. Notabene is growing fast—and we’re looking for people like you to help shape the future rails of the crypto industry!

The Impact You'll Have: 

Every crypto transfer we touch moves between institutions that run their own systems, answer to different regulators, and have no reason to trust each other. The software in the middle has to be right every time. A message processed twice, a lost update, or a record shown to the wrong tenant is a compliance failure for our customers.

You’ll work on the core platform that carries this data between institutions around the world, written in Go.

As a Staff Engineer on the team you’ll build the hardest parts of it, contribute to its design, and help the engineers around you do their best work.

What You'll Do 

- 
Design and build core parts of our transaction platform.

- 
Build for correctness under failure, with the isolation and auditability a regulated product needs.

- 
Scale the platform as transaction volume and the number of institutions per node grow, keeping latency predictable and the database healthy.

- 
Write design docs for what you build, and give sharp, useful reviews on other people’s designs and code.

- 
Build with AI agents every day, and help improve the specs, context and review practices that make agent-written code safe to ship in a regulated product.

- 
Work with product, compliance and customer-facing teams to turn regulatory and customer needs into working software.

- 
Own what you ship in production, from tracing and alerts to incident follow-ups.

- 
Mentor engineers on the team.

- 
Work on an on call rotation

Must Haves 

- 
Systems design depth. You’ve designed and owned distributed systems where correctness matters more than features. You know asynchronous processing well and can reason about what happens when parts of it fail.

- 
Strong Go, or deep production experience in another statically typed backend language (Java, Kotlin, Rust, C#) and the appetite to be shipping Go within your first weeks.

- 
PostgreSQL in depth: schema design, query plans, locking and isolation levels, migrations on live systems, and multi-tenant data.

- 
End-to-end ownership in the cloud. Working knowledge of AWS or GCP: IAM, networking, managed databases, queues and storage. You can read and change Terraform and debug production from traces and logs.

- 
AI-native engineering. You use coding agents such as Claude Code or Cursor every day and can show how. You write the specs and context, break work down for them, and review their output as hard as a human pull request. You know where they fail.

- 
Staff-level experience. A track record of delivering large, technically hard projects end to end and helping the engineers around you get better. Typically 8+ years building backend systems.

- 
Clear, concise writing in a remote company that makes decisions in documents and async threads.

- 
Security fundamentals for sensitive data: encryption in transit and at rest, key handling, minimising personal data, and least-privilege access.

Nice-to-Haves 

- 
Applied cryptography: encryption, signing and key management.

- 
Decentralized identity: DIDs, verifiable credentials, DIDComm.

- 
Regulated finance, payments or compliance: Travel Rule, AML, ISO 20022.

- 
Building and running software under SOC 2 or ISO 27001 controls.

- 
Crypto and blockchain knowledge: chains, addresses, assets, CAIP identifiers.

- 
Node.js and TypeScript.

- 
Queue and workflow systems, and modern observability tooling.

Benefits 

- 
Flexible Remote Work: Work from anywhere!

- 
$1000 WFH Stipend: Use within your first year of employment.

- 
MacBook Pro: Procured by you and your manager to find a model that meets your needs.

- 
Unlimited PTO: We trust you to take as much holiday as you need.

- 
Country-Specific Benefits: Statutory offerings and contributions, managed via our employer-of-record.

Apply Today! 

If you strongly believe this role is for you, please apply. Notabene considers a broad array of candidates, including those without blockchain experience. Whether you’re returning to work after a gap in employment, or taking the next step in your career path, we will be glad to have you on our radar. 

Notabene is proud to be an equal employment workplace and an affirmative action employer. By valuing inclusion and diversity of all forms, we strictly prohibit and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, ancestry, citizenship, sexual orientation, status as a protected veteran, or any other legally protected characteristic.

title: Staff Software Engineer (Journeys)
description:
1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

About engineering at Headway: 

- 
Building a new mental healthcare system at Headway is only possible because of the scale and leverage that software can provide. The engineering team at Headway is a small but mighty team using technology to build that future (and have a fun time while doing it!).

Principles that guide us:

- 
Focus on the mission : We view software as a means of effecting change in the world, not as an end unto itself. We write software to empower our patients and therapists to better solve the problems they’re facing.

- 
Ship small, learn fast : We are building new and novel products and believe that we learn what our users need by quickly shipping and iteration

- 
Everything is a product : Whether it's our patient search experience or a developer productivity improvement, we treat everything we build at Headway as a product with end-users in mind.

- 
Optimize for trust : We believe that engineers should be continually learning. To learn effectively and to be productive, engineers must feel safe asking questions and discussing mistakes.

Tools we use: 

- 
Languages: Python 3, TypeScript

- 
Libraries & Frameworks: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, React, Remix, Next.js

- 
Datastores: Postgres, Redis

- 
Infrastructure: AWS (Fargate, ECS, S3, and more), Spark and Kafka

- 
Monitoring: Datadog, PagerDuty, Sentry

- 
Version Control: Github, PagerDuty

- 
Vulnerability Management : Snyk, Semgrep

- 
Cloud Security: Lacework

- 
Delivery : Knock (transactional + product notifications), Iterable (lifecycle marketing + campaigns), Twilio, Mailgun

About the Journey Team at Headway 

- 
The Journey team powers how Headway reaches every patient and provider at the right moment, on the right channel - email, SMS and other communication channels. We’re building the next chapter: an agentic communications engine that learns which message, which channel, and which timing works best for each person — and gets smarter with every send. We own the full stack: from the delivery layer (Knock for transactional, Iterable for lifecycle), to the decision engine we’re building today.

About this role 

- 
We’re looking for a Staff Engineer to be the technical anchor of the Journey team. This is a senior IC role — the person who owns the architecture of how Headway communicates at scale. You’ll design and evolve the decision engine, experimentation layer, and channel orchestration that will define how Headway reaches patients and providers for years to come. You’ll set the technical direction for a multi-vendor communications stack, own the unified message ledger, and bring LLM-powered personalization from concept to production.

- 
This role is high-leverage and cross-functional. You’ll work closely with marketing, CX, product, and the patient org — and your work will directly impact patient acquisition, retention, and health outcomes.

Who you are:

- 
We’re looking for experienced engineers who have the ability to deal with ambiguity and learn new technologies and systems. Below are some additional experiences we think help engineers succeed at Headway.

- 
A systems thinker who holds the architecture of a complex, multi-vendor platform and guides the team through it

- 
An engineer who has shipped high-throughput, event-driven systems in production and knows what reliability requires

- 
A communicator who translates technical trade-offs for non-technical stakeholders and drives alignment across marketing, product, and engineering

- 
Genuinely excited about the intersection of AI and communications — and thoughtful about what makes AI-in-the-loop systems reliable at scale

- 
A leader who earns influence through technical depth and leaves teams more capable than they found them

Experience we’re seeking

- 
8+ years of software engineering experience, with meaningful time at Staff-level or equivalent

- 
Designed and built high-volume, event-driven communications platforms — email, SMS, push, or equivalent — at millions of events per month

- 
Fluency with multi-vendor delivery stacks; strong opinions about build-vs-buy trade-offs at the platform layer

- 
Experience building or working closely with experimentation infrastructure — A/B testing, engagement analytics, personalization, or recommendation systems

- 
Exposure to LLM-powered systems in production — not just API consumption, but thinking about reliability, latency, and quality at scale

- 
Demonstrated ability to shape technical direction across teams without direct authority

Comprehensive benefits: 

Medical, dental, vision, HSA/FSA, 401(k) including match for 2027!, Carrot Fertility reimbursement, and paid parental, medical and caregiver leave.

All in on agentic development

They make agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer works, and they can tell the difference between a demo and a system a team can rely on.

Practical engineering

The technical voice in new business

Hardware sense

The garden3d technology story 

Across the collective, they decide which tools and platforms we bet on, how every studio uses agents, and which internal tools are worth turning into products. When someone at garden3d asks "how should we build this?", this person has the answer, or knows who does.

Culture

title: Product Frontend Engineer
description:
quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app. 

quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end.

Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll.

The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters. 

Where this is going 

Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either.

That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience.

One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy.

Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled. 

Why this role exists 

Today , quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with.

What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards.

That is the opening. 

How we work 

We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing.

We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way.

And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high.

Tasks

What you will own 

Everything on the screen:

- The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account.

- The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components.

- The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device.

- Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native.

- The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished.

Where design ends, engineering begins. 

We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you.

Requirements

Who we are looking for 

You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed.

You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building.

You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels.

You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does.

Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works.

The Team 

We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action.

This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally.

- Background in robotics, automotive, aerospace or other hardware-related engineering environments

title: Senior Product Manager, App o11y | Germany  | Remote
description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X . 

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a fully remote position and we're considering candidates in Germany.

About Product Management: 

As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs, you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain. You will own your product’s roadmap, collateral, and market research, and you will collaborate with Grafana leadership on fine-tuning your product’s goals. You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders. The teams and people you will be interacting with will be 100% remote and globally distributed, so strong and proactive communication is essential.

Product Managers are the bridge that connect Engineering, Design, and UX to GTM. You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers. 

The opportunity: 

As the Product Manager for Application Observability (App O11y), you’ll be responsible for helping application developers and SREs understand how their applications are performing, what’s affecting their users, and where to focus when something goes wrong. You’ll continue to build App O11y on top of the Knowledge Graph and fully integrate high-fidelity signals like traces and profiles, making all three first-class parts of the product experience. You’ll bring these capabilities together into our full-stack observability experience, alongside our Drilldown products, while building AI-first workflows that help customers investigate issues, understand root cause, and take action beyond static experiences. 

Your primary responsibility will be to define the vision and roadmap that takes App O11y into its next wave of adoption and revenue growth. This will require heavy customer discovery, using product data to understand where users get stuck, and working with your engineering and design partners to turn those needs into clear priorities. You’ll balance new product opportunities with the depth, performance, and reliability customers need from tracing and profiling, while working across R&D to ensure App O11y is tightly woven into our broader Grafana Cloud suite.

You’ll also work closely with PMM and GTM to help customers understand the value of App O11y. This includes shaping pricing and packaging that make it easy to get started and grow with the product. You’ll regularly review customer feedback and usage data to understand what’s working and where people get stuck, and then be accountable for turning what you learn into stronger adoption and revenue growth.

As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs, you will:

- Transform ideas and feedback into a product vision and roadmap

- Empathize with customer problems in order to collect user needs, requirements, and pain points

- Curate and properly represent user feedback to Engineering, while providing evidence to support tradeoffs and priorities 

- Work closely with PMM to enable GTM on product differentiation, including creating and updating presentations, documentation, website content, datasheets, and whitepapers. 

- Use your deep product expertise to make decisions about our go-to-market strategies, pricing, packaging, licensing and tiering.

What You’ll Be Doing: 

- Transform ideas and feedback into a product vision and roadmap

- Empathize with customer problems in order to collect user needs, requirements, and pain points

- Curate and properly represent user feedback to Engineering, while providing evidence to support tradeoffs and priorities 

- Work closely with PMM to enable GTM on product differentiation, including creating and updating presentations, documentation, website content, datasheets, and whitepapers. 

- Use your deep product expertise to make decisions about our go-to-market strategies, pricing, packaging, licensing and tiering

What makes you a great fit: 

- A BS/BA in Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent work experience

- 5+ years of experience in Product Management

- 5+ years of experience in a B2B SaaS product 

- Experience using or building observability products, telemetry databases, and/or developer tools, either as a practitioner or for external customers

- A strong understanding of application architectures and distributed systems, with the ability to discuss tradeoffs in telemetry ingestion, storage, querying, and the workflows built on top

- Experience working with Engineering and Design teams to build delightful products and features with sound UX in a fast-paced environment

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders

Bonus Points: 

- Experience with OpenTelemetry, application instrumentation, SDKs, and telemetry collectors

- Experience with distributed tracing or continuous profiling systems, such as Grafana Tempo or Grafana Pyroscope

- Experience with eBPF and/or automatic instrumentation

- Experience with open source software and/or commercial open source companies

- Experience defining or evolving pricing and packaging for consumption-based or product-led SaaS offerings

- Experience operating applications in production, being on call, or troubleshooting performance and reliability issues

In Germany, the base compensation range for this role is EUR 99,945 - EUR 119,934 . Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally. 

*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process. 

Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs: 

- 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.

- Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.

- Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.

- Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.

- Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.

- Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.

- Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.

- Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.

- Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.

- In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it. 

- Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable. 

Equal Opportunity Employer: Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. We believe that equality and diversity build a strong organisation, and we work hard to ensure that is the foundation of our organisation as we grow. 

Grafana Labs may utilize AI tools in its recruitment process to assist in matching information provided in CVs to job postings. The recruitment team will continue to review inbound CVs manually to identify alignment with current openings.

title: Product Engineer, Shop
description:
ABOUT INSIFY 

We sell a mix of insurance products to small businesses (SME's) in the Netherlands, Germany and France, and we are in the process of scaling into more markets. 

Insurance infrastructure is brutal to get right. Every carrier has its own spec, every product its own underwriting rules, every country its own regulatory requirements. Most insurers throw people and process at that complexity - one-off integrations, workarounds on workarounds. We're building it differently: our insurance platform is where we consolidate that complexity, so that launching a new product or market becomes a configuration exercise rather than a rebuild.

Insify is a high-growth scale-up backed by more than €40M from investors like Accel, Munich Re Ventures, and Formula 1 champion Nico Rosberg. In five years we've expanded from the Netherlands into France and Germany. Our mission: become the European leader in AI-powered SME insurance.

About the role 

You would join the Shop team, responsible for everything that happens after a small business buys a policy from us. You would help shape how the platform handles the next product and the next country, on a system already carrying live policies and real customers.

The team owns end-to-end policy lifecycle management (mid-term adjustments, automated renewals, cancellations, and payment flows) alongside the backoffice tooling that gives our operations and support teams full visibility and control. We work closely with the Claims Team, and with the Activation Teams that turn a lead into a paying customer. Product and engineering together are 30+ people.

Every country has its own regulatory quirks, and every insurance product has unique data structures, lifecycle rules, and money flows.

As we expand across Europe, our goal isn't to write custom glue code for every new launch. It's to design elegant, reusable platform abstractions. We're building a system where introducing a new country or product feels like snapping modular building blocks together.

You're joining at an exciting inflection point: we have real traction, proven scale, and you get to directly build the foundational platform that powers our next wave of European growth.

What you'll be doing 

- Owning end-to-end the discovery and delivery of crucial platform features that enable our ability to scale as an insurance business

- Continuously and relentlessly seeking opportunities to turn new product demands into platform capabilities and features that scale across countries and insurance product lines

- Challenging our ideas and bringing your own. We encourage each other to act this way, so you can expect the same from others

What you'll need 

- 3+ years building complex web applications and services, with real production ownership

- Ownership & impact instinct - when needed you go beyond your direct stack to get to results, be that data / backend / frontend

- You get real leverage out of AI in your daily work, and you can say where it helped, and where it hurt

- Strong fundamentals in domain-driven design & service oriented architecture

Not all of the above are hard requirements. If you're strong on most of these and eager to grow into the rest, we'd still love to hear from you.

Nice to have 

- Experience building B2B products, especially in insurance & fintech

- Experience working on a product distributed across different country markets

- Strong observability instincts. You know where things will break, and can help others learn that too

Our stack 

TypeScript across the board, running on AWS (IaaC), in a single monorepo. If you have not worked with all of it, that is fine. We care more about how you reason about systems than about which tools you have used before.

We offer 

- Competitive compensation that reflects responsibility and impact. For this role the range is €65,000 to €85,000.

- Trust and autonomy. You'll have real ownership, room to make decisions, and space to shape your role as Insify evolves.

- Hybrid working. 3 days in the office, 2 from home, up to 4 weeks a year working from abroad, and 25 holiday days.

- Pension. We contribute 6% for you.

- Alleo budget. €50 net a month to spend on whatever you want, from the gym to takeaway. It rolls over if you don't use it.

- Learning and coaching. Internal leadership programs, and coaching to go with them.

- A central Amsterdam office. Shared lunches, dogs, whiteboards, and Friday drinks.

- Hardware & setup. A high-spec MacBook Pro, high-res monitors at the office, and comfortable ergonomic seating.

title: Cloud Systems Administrator
description:
Headquarters: 

URL: https://oneimaging.com 

Radiology is the second most used healthcare service, used by over 51% of the workforce annually. Despite the critical role of radiology in healthcare, the process for undergoing a medical imaging exam has remained unchanged for decades. OneImaging is solving this with a concierge approach and a premium-quality radiology network of over 5,000 vetted providers across 48 states, which also reduces imaging costs by 60-80%. Our solution helps patients and families access essential radiology services at fair prices and without surprise bills, all while delivering immediate savings and ROI for employers and payers on every exam.

The Systems Administrator owns the day-to-day administration of our SaaS and cloud vendor stack, with security and logging as the first priority. You will manage user access across every platform we use, keep audit logging and security controls configured and reviewed, write scripts to automate repetitive admin work, and act as a first responder on security incidents. You will also provide hands-on IT support to employees. This is a generalist role for someone who likes owning systems end to end: you are the person who knows how each vendor is set up, who has access to what, and where the logs live. 

What you'll do: 

Vendor and SaaS administration (security and logging first) 

- Serve as the primary administrator for our SaaS and cloud platforms: tenant settings, SSO/SAML and SCIM integration, MFA enforcement, API keys, roles and permissions.

- Configure and maintain audit logging on every platform that supports it; centralize logs where possible and make sure retention meets our compliance needs.

- Run periodic access reviews, remove stale accounts and over-privileged roles, and keep an accurate inventory of who has admin rights where.

- Own the security posture of each vendor: review security settings on new tools before rollout, track vendor security notices, and evaluate new vendor requests for risk.

User lifecycle and identity

- Onboard and offboard employees and contractors across all systems the same day, driven from Rippling and Google Workspace, our identity sources of truth.

- Manage groups, roles and licenses; keep license counts right-sized and flag waste.

- Maintain device enrollment, MDM policies and endpoint security for company laptops.

Scripting and automation

- Write and maintain scripts (Python, PowerShell, Bash) and use vendor APIs to automate provisioning, access reviews, log collection and reporting.

- Build lightweight integrations between systems (for example, HRIS to identity provider to SaaS) so manual admin work shrinks over time.

Security incident response

- Act as a first responder on security alerts: triage, contain (disable accounts, revoke tokens, isolate devices), gather evidence from logs, and escalate.

- Participate in post-incident reviews and implement the fixes that come out of them.

- Help maintain and test our incident response and business continuity runbooks.

IT support

- Provide tier 1–2 support to employees: hardware, accounts, access, video conferencing, printers and office network.

- Procure, image and manage laptops and peripherals; keep an asset inventory current.

- Write and keep up internal how-to documentation so common requests become self-service.

Platforms you will administer

These are our largest software and cloud vendors by spend over the last 12 months. Deep experience with the first group is expected; the rest you will pick up on the job.

Area

Platforms

Cloud infrastructure

Amazon Web Services (IAM, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Security Hub)

Identity, HR and devices

Rippling (HRIS, SSO, device management) and Google Workspace, used together as our identity source of truth

Productivity and email

Google Workspace (admin console, Vault, security center)

Customer support and CRM

Zendesk, Salesforce, Intercom

Communications

Zoom, Aircall, Twilio

Data and engineering

Databricks, MongoDB Atlas, Sentry, Linear, Postman, Stytch

AI platforms

Anthropic, OpenAI (API key and usage management)

Collaboration and design

Notion, Lucid, Figma, Adobe, Scribe

Security tools

NordVPN Teams, Virtru (email encryption)

Healthcare operations

Waystar, AdvancedMD

Marketing and recruiting

Braze, ActiveCampaign, Greenhouse, LinkedIn

About you: 

- 3+ years administering SaaS and cloud platforms in a company of 50–500 people, including Google Workspace and an identity/HR platform like Rippling or Okta, and ideally AWS.

- Hands-on experience configuring SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, MFA policies and role-based access.

- Working knowledge of audit logging and log review: you know what a CloudTrail event, a Workspace audit log or a Zendesk audit entry looks like and what to do with it.

- Scripting ability in at least one of Python, PowerShell or Bash, and comfort calling REST APIs.

- Experience responding to security incidents (phishing, compromised accounts, lost devices) and documenting what happened.

- Strong IT support instincts: you communicate clearly with non-technical colleagues and close tickets fast.

- Familiarity with HIPAA or a comparable compliance framework (SOC 2, ISO 27001) and what it means for access control and logging.

Nice to have:

- AWS Certified SysOps Administrator, Security Specialty, or Google Workspace Administrator certification.

- Experience with a SIEM or log aggregation tool (Datadog, Splunk, Google SecOps, or similar) and writing detection rules.

- MDM experience (Rippling, Jamf, Kandji, Intune) and macOS/Windows endpoint hardening.

- Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code for managing AWS and SaaS configuration.

- Prior work in a healthcare or other regulated company.

- Experience administering API usage and keys for AI platforms (Anthropic, OpenAI) and setting spend and access controls.

The base salary range for this position is $60,000 - $75,000. Individual compensation will depend on various factors, including qualifications, skills, experience, location, and applicable laws. In addition to base salary, this role is eligible to participate in our equity incentive and competitive benefits plans.

title: QA Engineer (Anywhere in Europe)
description:
The Role We Need: 

PadSplit is hiring a QA Engineer to strengthen quality across our Marketplace pod, spanning Mobile (iOS/Android), Web, and backend Platform systems. As our product complexity increases, we need someone who can independently validate cross-platform user flows, reduce production risk, and increase release confidence through disciplined, hands-on testing.

The Person We Are Looking For: 

We’re looking for a proactive, technically fluent QA Engineer who thrives in a dynamic startup environment and takes ownership of product quality. You’re comfortable working across mobile, web, and backend systems, partnering closely with Engineering and Product to identify risk early, and prevent issues before they reach production.

Here’s What You’ll Do Day-To-Day:

- Test Strategy Ownership – Design and execute comprehensive test strategies across Mobile, Web, and backend services.

- End-to-End Validation – Validate complex user flows that span frontend interfaces and backend systems.

- API & Backend Testing – Perform API validation, data integrity checks, and business logic testing.

- Regression Coverage – Execute cross-platform regression testing prior to releases to ensure stability.

- Issue Investigation – Diagnose defects using logs, network tools, and API inspection techniques.

- Defect Lifecycle Management – Document, prioritize, and track defects while partnering with engineers on root-cause resolution.

- Environment Management – Maintain test environments, device coverage, and reliable platform test data.

- Risk Identification – Proactively surface quality risks during sprint planning and release cycles.

Here’s What You’ll Need To Be Successful:

- Cross-Platform Testing Experience – Demonstrated experience testing Mobile, Web, and/or backend systems.

- API Validation Expertise – Strong experience validating RESTful APIs and backend business logic.

- SDLC/STLC Knowledge – Solid understanding of software and testing lifecycle best practices.

- Testing Tool Proficiency – Hands-on experience with API testing tools such as Postman (or similar platforms).

- Technical Acumen – Ability to understand system architecture, integrations, and data flow.

- Startup Adaptability – Comfortable operating in a remote, fast-paced, and evolving environment.

- Ownership Mindset – High level of accountability with strong independent execution.

- Clear Communication – Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

Interview Process:

- Your application will be reviewed for possible next steps by the Hiring Manager.

- If you meet eligibility requirements, the next step would be a video interview with a member of the PeopleOps team for about thirty (30) minutes.

- If warranted, the next step would be a technical video interview with our QA Lead and QA Engineer for one (1) hour

- If warranted, the next step would be a final live technical assessment with our QA Lead and QA Engineer for one (1) hour

- If warranted, then we move to contract!

Compensation is based on the role's scope, national market benchmarks, the person's expertise and experience, and the impact of their contributions to our business goals.

description:
What you’ll do 

We are looking for a Principal Machine Learning Engineer to join the DS & AI organization at Doctolib. This is a transversal force multiplier role operating across all AI teams: Clinical, Productivity, Phone Assistant and ASR. Rather than working within a single feature team, you will own the cross-cutting technical challenges: defining how Doctolib's product and AI teams build agentic solutions, standardizing ML evaluation frameworks, and spreading strong engineering practices across the org. You will unblock teams, shape architecture decisions, and take on the deep technical work that requires senior ML judgment at scale, directly impacting the daily lives of 400,000 healthcare professionals and the health of 80 million patients. Building at Doctolib means delivering innovative products that measurably improve outcomes for care teams and patients alike.

Technical Strategy & Architecture 

- Own cross-team ML architecture decisions, from model selection to production deployment patterns and strategic build vs. buy decisions

- Define and drive adoption of rigorous evaluation frameworks across all AI teams, setting the standard for how Doctolib measures model and agentic performance

- Establish shared production infrastructure patterns for AI: model and prompt versioning, guardrails, uncertainty quantification, cost optimization, and observability

- Lead the technical design of agentic solutions and define how product teams across Doctolib build on top of AI capabilities

- Elevate technical standards across the DS & AI org by influencing Staff and Senior ML Engineers through architecture reviews, technical guidance, and practice propagation

- Partner with Product, Legal, and Compliance teams to ensure safe rollout and meet EU regulatory expectations (GDPR, MDR, EU AI Act)

Who you are 

Before you read on, if you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

You'll be a great fit if:

- You have 10+ years in ML/AI with 3+ years at Staff+ or Principal level leading complex, multi-team technical initiatives

- You have deep expertise in at least two of: clinical NLP, LLM fine-tuning and evaluation, automatic speech recognition, RAG systems, or reinforcement learning

- You are expert in Python, PyTorch/Transformers for training, and vLLM for inference with a track record deploying ML systems in production (AWS/GCP)

- You have a PhD in Computer Science, AI, Statistics, or related field (or equivalent research experience)

- You have exceptional communication skills and are able to align diverse stakeholders and explain complex technical decisions

Now it would be fantastic if you have:

- Publications in top-tier ML/AI conferences (NeurIPS, ICLR, ACL) or medical informatics venues

- Experience with EU healthcare regulations (GDPR, MDR, AI Act)

- Prior work with clinical data or healthcare applications

Life at Doctolib Tech 

- Our solutions are built on a single fully cloud-native platform supporting web and mobile interfaces across multiple languages and healthcare specialties.

- Our stack includes Rails, TypeScript, Java, Python, Kotlin, Swift, and React Native.

- We leverage AI ethically to empower patients and professionals. Discover our AI vision here .

Want to learn more about our tech culture and environment? Visit the Doctolib Tech site . 

What we offer 

- A Deutschlandticket (Germany-wide public transport pass) fully paid for by Doctolib

- 28 vacation days + 1 additional day for each full calendar year of employment (up to a maximum of 30 days)

- Work from abroad for up to 10 days per year thanks to our flexibility days policy

- Company health insurance with great supplementary benefits through our partner Allianz

- Company pension scheme (bAV) through Allianz with an employer subsidy of 40% (15% within the probationary period)

- The Doctolib Parent Care program, which includes one month additional parental leave and much more

- Enrollment in Doctolib's long-term employee value sharing plan called DoctoGrowth

- Free mental health and coaching services through our partner Moka.care

- Subsidized sports membership through our partner Urban Sports Club

- A flexible workplace policy offering both hybrid and office-based mode

- Alongside healthy snacks and our regular breakfast buffet, we provide a subsidized meal benefit

- For caregivers and workers with disabilities, a package including an adaptation of the remote policy, extra days off for medical reasons, and psychological support

- Relocation support in case of international mobility

- Access to the best AI tools for coding, development and dedicated training

The interview process 

- HR Screen

- Hiring Manager Interview

- System Design Interview

- Behavioral Interview

- Case Study

- At least one reference check

We want your experience to be clear, respectful, and transparent. Learn more on our candidate experience page .

Job details 

- Permanent position

- Full-time

- Berlin

- Hybrid work mode (up to 2 remote days per week)

- Start date: as soon as possible

We welcome everyone 

At Doctolib, we believe in improving access to healthcare for everyone - regardless of where you come from or what you look like. We evaluate candidates based solely on qualifications and motivation, without any form of discrimination. We respect and celebrate diversity! 

The more diverse ideas are heard, the more our product will truly improve healthcare for all. You are welcome to apply regardless of gender, religion, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity, disability, or place of origin. 

To ensure equal opportunities, we invite you to exclude personal information (e.g., pictures, age) from your applications. If you have a disability, let us know if there's any way we can make the interview process smoother for you! Join us in building the healthcare we all dream of. 

Your data privacy 

All information transmitted via this form is processed by Doctolib for application management. For more on how we process your data, click here . For inquiries or to exercise your rights, contact us at hr.dataprivacy(at)doctolib.com.

description:
IT Internship - Cloud-Native Platform Engineering & Developer Experience (AnyOrg) 

Becoming an IT professional that you aspire to be 

About the Internship 

Swisscom is always keen on attracting and developing the best talents. As part of the leading telecom and tech company in Switzerland, you will work on real projects that have real impact. From day one, you will be part of an international team collaborating across Switzerland, Rotterdam, and Riga, contributing to innovative solutions in Swisscom’s digital transformation. This means working hands‑on in backend, cloud, or full‑stack development, applying your Computer Science skills to real technical challenges.

With colleagues from over 60 nationalities, diversity is not just something we value, it is how we work. We believe in open collaboration, ownership, and continuous learning. You will be encouraged to share ideas, take initiative, and grow within the environment. We respect each other, help each other out, and are not afraid to make mistakes. We make sure you can be the best version of yourself.

Our internship program starts on 1st February 2027 . In this 6 months internship you will work in agile teams using Scrum and SAFe, gaining hands-on experience in a fast-paced and supportive environment.

About the Internship Project: 

Cloud-Native Platform Engineering & Developer Experience (AnyOrg) 

Join a team building enterprise platform services used by engineers across Swisscom. You will work on cloud-native Front/backed services, platform automation, CI/CD pipelines, developer tooling and security integrations. The project offers hands-on experience with modern software engineering practices, DevOps, GitLab pipelines and cloud technologies while collaborating with experienced engineers in an international Agile environment.

Must-haves: TypeScript; Git 
Nice-to-haves: Angular; AWS; Docker; Kubernetes; UX/UI; CSS

Who are you? 

- You are a student enrolled in the last year of your HBO or University program in the field of Computer Science, Informatica, or any other similar field.

- You live in the Netherlands. 

- You are willing to contribute to an international team and you have an agile mindset.

- You are curious and responsible.

- You have a good level of English; any other language is a plus.

Please note that for non-EU students, it is necessary to provide the NUFFIC Agreement for the 6-month internship from your university in order to be eligible. 

Perks 

- 810 € gross Monthly Allowance (Full time)

- IT Equipment

- Agile working environment and lean management instructor

- Flexible working time model

- Plenty of opportunities for training and personal development

- International Environment

- Holidays & time off

Contact 

Do you have any questions or do you want to know why we love working at Swisscom? Feel free to reach out to Lilla Egyed (

About WelcomeHome 

WelcomeHome is an Atlanta-based SaaS provider with the mission to build the best Customer Relationship Management (CRM) platform in the Senior Living and Home Care space. Since launch in 2019, we have sustained consistent and rapid growth, expanding from four to 100+ employees.

To date, we’ve succeeded with a focused team that prioritizes client success over external / VC reporting and updates.

WelcomeHome’s differentiation extends beyond providing the most technologically advanced, easy-to-use software in the space. Clients receive world class support, from the migration from their legacy CRM platform to ongoing day-to-day training and troubleshooting.

About the Role: 

WelcomeHome is looking for Senior Ruby on Rails Engineers excited about building user-friendly software solutions. This role is fully remote (based in the U.S.), will report to our VP of Engineering (based in Las Vegas), and play an integral role in product development and have the opportunity to impact several areas of the business.

Tech Stack 

- Backend: Ruby on Rails 8 / Ruby 3.3 (currently upgrading to Ruby 4)

- Frontend: Haml, Stimulus, minimal React (where it earns its place)

- Testing: Minitest + Capybara, TDD throughout

- Data/Async: PostgreSQL, Redis, Sidekiq

- Infrastructure: AWS (Aurora, S3, EC2) via Cloud66

- AI: Pi, Codex, and Claude Code used in the daily dev workflow

A great candidate might have: 

- Deep experience with Ruby on Rails

- 5+ years software engineering experience

- Passion for building high quality software focused on the user experience

- Ability to take ownership and work well with others

- Demonstrated ability to work independently to problem solve and offer solutions

- Experience using Claude Code (or comparable AI tools) as part of your daily development workflow

- Prior experience in a growth stage company or start-up

What You'll Get 

WelcomeHome values all of its employees and strives to provide a competitive compensation package. Benefits include health, vision and dental coverage, 401(k) matching, paid parental leave, and unlimited PTO.

But, on top of that, you'll be surrounded by awesome people who care deeply about what they do and will do whatever it takes to help you succeed

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/welcomehome-software-senior-software-engineer

title: Mid/Senior AI LLM Engineer (Full Remote - Netherlands)
description:
Our Vision & Products

🚀 EverAI — Building the Future of AI Companionship 

One of the Top 15 Largest & Fastest-Growing AI Companies in the World 

50 Million Users in 2 years — Help Us Reach 100M first, 500M next 

At EverAI , we’re shaping what it means to connect with AI. With 50 million users and counting , we're not just building products — we're creating entirely new categories.

Our flagship product is the world’s largest AI companionship platform , redefining relationships for millions. It is governed by our proprietary moderation system, EverGuard — an internal AI designed to ensure everything we build is safe, ethical, and human-first .

And we’re only just getting started! 

Our Team

We are an enthusiastic, passionate and hardworking team of ≈ 100 people. Our founding team has strong entrepreneurial experience building and scaling web products from 0 to IPO.

Alexis Soulopoulos [CEO]

• 10+ years in Tech Executive Leadership 

• Co-Founder Mad Paws Holdings (from 0 to IPO) 

• Forbes 30 under 30 + Deloitte TechFast50 ’22 & ‘23 

Michael Monin [Co-founder & CTO]

• 10+ years as CTO / COO (web2/web3), 3 years in AI/LLM 

• Serial-entrepreneur: MTK Digital (exited / 0->$20m revenue) and Zipchat (AI Chatbot for E-commerce brands) 

Thomas Lacroix [Co-founder & CMO]

• 8+ years in Customer Acquisition & E-commerce Growth 

• Serial-entrepreneur: Curatible (sold to Blackstone) and MTK Digital (exited / 0->$20m revenue) 

Maruša Fasano [CFO/Legal]

• 25+ years in Finance, Strategy, M&A 

• Ex-CFO/M&A @Curatible (exited to Blackstone) 

• Ex-President of the Board @SotremoSA (exited) 

• Co-founder/CFO @SoftOne (exited) 

Your Role

Most LLM roles stop at experimentation.

Here, the models you improve power experiences for 50M+ users. 

Most of our traffic runs on self-hosted, fine-tuned open-weight models . On our internal roleplay evals, our smaller fine-tuned models can outperform much larger off-the-shelf models. Your job is to make them better. 

You’ll join a small AI team led by Marco, our LLM Tech Lead , working closely with our CTO, Product, Web and DevOps teams. You’ll work across data, post-training, evals, and model behavior, taking ideas from failure analysis to production.

The problems are real: personalization, character consistency, long conversations, better evals, multilingual behavior, and faster training cycles. 

If you want to shape model behavior at consumer scale, this is the role. 

Key Responsibilities

- Fine-tune open-weight LLMs using SFT, LoRA/QLoRA and post-training methods such as DPO and GRPO

- Diagnose model failures and turn them into experiments. Decide whether the answer is better data, post-training, prompting or classifiers

- Build training data and evals that directly shape what gets trained next

- Improve model behavior across personalization, consistency, tone, multilingual and group interactions

- Ship to production and use real user behavior to guide the next iteration

- Speed up the training loop so experiments are faster, easier to compare, and more reproducible

Your Qualifications

- You’ve personally post-trained open-weight LLMs for a user-facing product and shipped them to production

- You’ve worked where AI was core to the product or business , not an experimental side feature

- Fine-tuning is core to your experience

- Strong Python, PyTorch and Hugging Face , with hands-on GPU training and debugging

- You build data and evals yourself and make decisions from evidence

- You can take work beyond notebooks into production 

- You use AI tools daily in your own engineering work

- You are fully comfortable working with uncensored models and explicit NSFW content , including harmful material when developing and evaluating moderation system

Bonus points

- Experience with conversational AI, roleplay products, or highly personalized consumer AI

- Multilingual LLMs

- Moderation, safety, or adversarial testing

- Multimodal models

- Open-source LLM / post-training contributions

Why EverAI?

📈 Exponential Growth : From 50M users in 2 years, to 100M next — and 500M beyond

🚀 Track Record of Category-Creating Innovation : We consistently launch world-first AI applications — setting the pace, not following it

🌍 Global Impact : Top-tier user growth, real-world adoption, and cultural relevance

🧠 Proven Leadership : A senior team that’s launched, scaled, and exited & IPO’d multiple scale ups — now fully focused on reshaping AI companionship

👥 Elite Remote Team : 100% remote and built to win — world-class talent from Tier 1 tech companies , with a culture of ownership, velocity, and radical creativity

🛡️ Ethical Core : Our AI ecosystem is governed by EverGuard, our proprietary AI moderation technology , ensuring responsible development at scale

What We Offer

✍️ Contract Type: We prefer B2B, but we’re flexible, what matters is long-term commitment and impact
📍 Work From Anywhere: Fully remote. Choose the environment where you do your best work
🏝️ Paid Time Off: 4 weeks (20 working days) of PTO per year to recharge and reset
👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Annual Gathering: A yearly in-person meetup to connect, brainstorm, and celebrate wins together
❤️‍🩹 Health & Wellness Support: Monthly allowance of 100 USD for health insurance expenses & access to unlimited 1:1 sessions with psychologists and lifestyle experts through OpenUp (also available to up to three of your family members)
🏢 Co-Working Space Budget: Work from a co-working space up to twice per month (35 EUR / 40 USD per visit) to stay inspired and connected
📚 Learning Budget: Dedicated funds to support your professional growth: courses, books, conferences, events, or certifications
💻 Company Laptop & Equipment: Laptop provided + monitor budget up to 250 USD + keyboard/mouse/mic/headphones budget up to 150 USD
⚡ AI Tools Access: Premium access to ChatGPT, Hugging Face, Claude Code, and any other tool needed to excel at your job, power your ideas and workflows

🎯 Top Tier Talent Is Our Multiplier

We’re a fully remote group of A-players from Tier 1 tech , led by an exec team who’ve launched, scaled, and exited multiple companies . We move fast, and care deeply about what we build — and who we build it with.

We’re looking for exceptional talent ready to ship & distribute world-first AI products at scale, fast, and co-create with us this category-defining business.

If that’s you — reach out and apply! 

Compensation: €75K – €125K

- • Annual Compensation Range (Gross) €75K – €125K

title: Staff Software Engineer - Experimentation
description:
1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

About engineering at Headway 

Building a new mental healthcare system at Headway is only possible because of the scale and leverage that software can provide. The engineering team at Headway is a small but mighty team using technology to build that future (and have a fun time while doing it!).

Principles that guide us: 

- 
Focus on the mission: We view software as a means of effecting change in the world, not as an end unto itself. We write software to empower our patients and therapists to better solve the problems they're facing.

- 
Ship small, learn fast: We are building new and novel products and believe that we learn what our users need by quickly shipping and iteration

- 
Everything is a product: Whether it's our patient search experience or a developer productivity improvement, we treat everything we build at Headway as a product with end-users in mind.

- 
Optimize for trust: We believe that engineers should be continually learning. To learn effectively and to be productive, engineers must feel safe asking questions and discussing mistakes.

Tools we use: 

- 
Languages: Python 3, TypeScript

- 
Libraries & Frameworks: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, React, Remix

- 
Experimentation & Analytics: LaunchDarkly, Statsig, dbt, Snowflake

- 
Datastores: Postgres, Redis

- 
Infrastructure: AWS (Fargate, ECS, S3, and more), Cloudflare, Spark and Kafka

- 
Monitoring: Datadog, PagerDuty, Sentry

- 
Version Control: Github

About the role 

We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to own how Headway runs experiments. "Ship small, learn fast" is the second principle on the list above, and experimentation is how we actually do it: eleven teams have run hundreds of experiments deciding how patients find a therapist, how quickly new providers get up and running, whether our AI products are working, and how we collect the clinical outcomes data that proves care is effective. You will own the platform all of that runs on.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role with unusually wide reach. You will design and build the core primitives, including how users are assigned to experiments, how we record what someone actually saw, and how we recognize the same person across devices and between browsing anonymously and signing in. You will decide what our long-term experimentation and feature flagging stack should be; we run LaunchDarkly and Statsig today, and that architecture is yours to evaluate and consolidate. You will also make AI a real part of the workflow, from validating an experiment's setup before it starts to catching a broken experiment automatically instead of discovering it in a Slack thread a week later.

You will also evolve our experimentation capabilities to expand into market-based testing. Headway is a multi-sided marketplace, so we frequently need to change something for therapists and measure what happens to patients, which changes both how a test must be designed and how it can be analyzed. We need to test whole geographic markets, not just individual users. We need to hold groups out for long stretches to understand real long-term impact. These capabilities are well understood in the industry and we have not built them yet, and they are the ones our business needs next.

The job is a platform and a program in equal measure. Half of it is the technical foundation. The other half is raising how well the whole company experiments: the defaults, the review, the documentation, and the education that let a team run a trustworthy experiment without needing you in the room. You will gather needs from teams who all want something different, sequence them into a roadmap, and say no clearly, which means acting as part technical product manager for your own platform.

You will sit in the Patient org, where the highest volume of experiments happens, and serve the whole company. Trustworthy results are shared ownership. You will own assignment, exposure, and the experiment data pipelines, which are the parts of the chain that are engineering problems. You will work closely with Data Science, who own statistical methodology, and with the teams who own our event tracking and metric definitions, because a number is only as trustworthy as the weakest link in that chain.

Who you are 

We are looking for a Staff level engineer who wants their impact measured by what other teams can now do. You think in systems, you are uncomfortable with numbers you cannot explain, and you raise the bar for the people around you.

- 
You have owned an experimentation or feature flagging stack end to end rather than only used one. Whether you built it from first principles or built the missing pieces on top of a vendor matters far less to us than having been accountable for whether the results were correct.

- 
You have built the parts that do not come out of the box: assignment that persists correctly, exposure that reflects what a user actually saw, identity resolved across sessions and devices, or the diagnostics that catch a broken experiment early.

- 
You are fluent enough in the statistics to be a real partner to data scientists. You can tell the difference between a result that is weak and a result that is invalid, and you can hold your position on a measurement question with someone who does this full time.

- 
You have debugged the hard class of measurement bugs: traffic that split unevenly, users who ended up in both arms, effects that vanished once you looked at who was actually exposed, identity that broke between anonymous and logged-in sessions.

- 
You have built a program and not only a platform. You have measurably raised how well an organization experiments through defaults, templates, review, and teaching, not only through code.

- 
You have made a build versus buy call on a platform and lived with it. You can reason about vendor risk and about where a warehouse-native approach beats a hosted one.

- 
You have landed a migration on teams that did not ask for one, by making the new path easier than the old path rather than by mandate.

- 
You use AI as genuine leverage in your work and you have clear opinions about where it must not be trusted without a human.

- 
You have driven technical direction beyond your own team through design documents, reviews, and planning cycles, and you regularly mentor senior engineers.

- 
You are willing to flex across the stack. This role touches backend services, front end rendering, CDN behavior, and the data warehouse.

- 
Experience with multi-sided marketplaces, growth or search and ranking systems, or healthcare is a plus, though none is required.

Compensation 

The expected base pay range for this position is $265,000-$331,000 , based on a variety of factors including qualifications, experience, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for an equity grant, depending on the position and level.

Comprehensive benefits: 

Medical, dental, vision, HSA/FSA, 401(k) including match for 2027!, Carrot Fertility reimbursement, and paid parental, medical and caregiver leave.

Headway is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Headway will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please inform the recruiter when they contact you to schedule your interview.

All official communication will come from a @ findheadway.com email address.
